caption: Brendan Ngwa Nforbi v. Swift Transportation Co. of Arizona LLC
court: USDC E.D. Cal. — Sacramento Division (proposed direct filing)
claims: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E)/(j)(4)(A) (I&B — preliminary NSOPW); ICRAA §§ 1786.40/1786.50; UCL § 17200
status: FEDERAL REDRAFT — E.D. Cal. Sacramento on § 1332 / § 1367; three counts (PC § 290.46, ICRAA, UCL). No FCRA count. No May 29. File on or before September 26, 2026. Inspection demands drafted but unsigned.
note: The September 8, 2026 verified San Joaquin packet is historical work product only; it never reached the clerk. Generate the live E.D. Cal. draft with internal/scripts/matter38-edca-complaint.py. File on or before September 26, 2026 if the pre-adverse is accrual. Diversity § 1332 / supplemental § 1367; do not invent LLC members or a wage rate. FCRA is reserved, not pleaded — 2023 letters closed the two-year clock and the role is Class A Driver. No May 29. Serve the current SOS agent (confirm NRAI), not a terminal. Do not publish the decrypted packet. Knight-Swift parent is not named. Asurint / Tenstreet / DriverIQ / Equifax are inspection targets, not defendants.
defendants: Swift Transportation Co. of Arizona LLC, a Delaware limited liability company, d/b/a Swift Transportation (USDOT 54283; 2200 South 75th Avenue, Phoenix, AZ 85043 on the Oct. 5 letter) is the proposed sole opening defendant. Knight-Swift Transportation Holdings, Inc. is not named merely as parent. Asurint, Tenstreet, DriverIQ/Cisive, and Equifax Work Number are named in Swift's own letter as report sources and remain nonparty inspection targets. Robin Kaufman and Matt Hutto are witnesses.
causes: [I&B ULTIMATE FACTS] Penal Code § 290.46(j)(2)(E), (j)(4)(A) — the in-process NSOPW component was drawing California Megan's Law / DOJ registry data and Swift used that preliminary output, in whole or in part, in the Class A Driver denial. Printed snapshots contain neither a completed hit nor a completed no-record and no California source-of-record line. NSOPW is not automatically § 290.46 information. Same-consumer comparators, if any, are one I&B sentence — not Swift's report. CCP § 338(a) from Sept. 26 / Oct. 5, 2023 (outer bound September 26, 2026 if pre-adverse is accrual).

[INDEPENDENT PATH] ICRAA, Civ. Code §§ 1786.40 and 1786.50 — October 5 letter names agencies and says consumer reports influenced the decision but does not give the investigative-report advice. Independent of a completed hit. § 1786.52 discovery date does not appear on the face. No May 29 date.
[INDEPENDENT / EQUITABLE] UCL § 17200 — unlawful and unfair prongs; four-year § 17208 clock; restitution of vested money/property only.

[FEDERAL ANCHOR] Diversity § 1332(a)(1) and supplemental § 1367 — Plaintiff is a California citizen; Swift is a Delaware LLC (SOS entity 201014710033; SEC Ex. 21.1 lists it as a Delaware subsidiary, not a membership roll); I&B no member is a California citizen; AIC pleaded in good faith from lost Class A employment according to proof plus Count 1 actual/additional/fee/exemplary remedies. Do not invent members or a wage. Do not use ICRAA's $10,000 or the optional $25,000 civil penalty to manufacture AIC. Rule 7.1 if Swift contests.
[OMITTED] CCRAA — October 5 letter recites a copy and Summary of Rights; reserve if a later-completed component was used and withheld.

[OMITTED] FCRA — two-year § 1681p clock from the 2023 FCRA letters closed in 2025; Class A Driver also presents a DOT § 1681b(b)(3)(B)–(C) defense. Reserved if production shows a timely claim those letters did not cure.
[OMITTED] Tameny / IIED / contract / FEHA — two-year clocks closed; no CRD; no written offer.
key_facts: The role was Class A Driver. On Sept. 22, 2023, Swift driver recruiters Robin Kaufman and Matt Hutto emailed Plaintiff through Tenstreet about completing a Class A Driver application. On Sept. 25, Tenstreet posted a DriverIQ employment document and an FMCSA Clearinghouse result; FMCSA emailed that SWIFT TRANSPORTATION CO OF ARIZONA LLC (USDOT 54283) had requested Clearinghouse access. On Sept. 26, Swift Recruiting emailed an encrypted pre-adverse letter, later decrypted. On Oct. 5, Swift sent a post-adverse letter stating it had decided not to employ Plaintiff based in whole or in part on consumer reports from Asurint, Tenstreet, DriverIQ, FMCSA-DOT, and Equifax Work Number. The decrypted packet is pleaded as known fact: National Criminal without Sex Offender Clear; federal criminal Clear; completed county criminal Clear; NSOPW remained Processing on every snapshot furnished to Plaintiff; the furnished packet contains neither a completed hit nor a completed no-record, and no California source-of-record line; Clearinghouse Driver Not Prohibited. Count 1 is I&B that the in-process NSOPW component was drawing California Megan's Law / DOJ registry data and that Swift used that preliminary output on October 5. The file does not contain a written offer, a terminal assignment, or a rate of pay. What the completed criminal / MVR / PSP / CDLIS components contain is not information disclosed pursuant to Penal Code § 290.46. Do not treat this packet as proof that Home Depot, Best Buy, or AT&T used the registry. Do not name Lerma in the complaint.
procedural_status: Pre-filing E.D. Cal. Sacramento redraft (L.R. 120(d)). The signed verified San Joaquin complaint dated September 8, 2026 was never clerk-filed. SMJ is § 1332 / § 1367; FCRA is not a count. File on or before September 26, 2026 if the pre-adverse is accrual (October 5, 2026 if post-adverse). Serve the current SOS agent; confirm NRAI. Unsigned Asurint / § 1198.5 demands are drafted. Remaining gates: Plaintiff signature, official JS-44 / AO-440 / AO-239, SOS confirmation, sending the inspection demands, and a walk-up before the § 338(a) outer bound.
damages: No wage rate or hours are in the record; those figures are not invented. Portfolio valuation remains the post-favorable-MTD settlement range: $45,000 / $65,000 / $90,000. Count 1 is the healthier statutory path. Contingent remedies: Penal Code § 290.46(j)(4)(A); ICRAA § 1786.50 actual damages or $10,000, whichever is greater; UCL restitution of vested money/property only. Diversity AIC is pleaded in good faith from lost Class A employment according to proof plus Count 1 actual/additional/fee/exemplary remedies. Do not use ICRAA's $10,000 floor or the optional $25,000 civil penalty to manufacture AIC. Do not invent a wage. Do not import UPS/Pilot numbers.
risk: NSOPW remained Processing, not a completed hit, and no California source-of-record line. Count 1 is I&B that the in-process NSOPW component was drawing California Megan's Law / DOJ registry data and that Swift used that preliminary output on October 5. NSOPW is not automatically § 290.46 information. If production shows a completed no-record and no preliminary use, Count 1 dies then; ICRAA/UCL do not need a hit. A 12(b)(1) fight on LLC membership or AIC is the federal cost of opening in Sacramento without a live FCRA count; if Count 1 fails, ICRAA's $10,000 does not get to $75,000. Do not invent members or a wage. CCP § 338(a) from Sept. 26, 2023 runs to September 26, 2026 — file that week. Do not plead FCRA. Do not plead May 29. Distinguish Lerma when they file an RJN; do not name it in the complaint.
